title: Crime, Punishment and Witchcraft
description:
This Halloween, discover a darker side of Scottish history at The Inverness Castle Experience.

Join The Witches of Scotland, Claire Mitchell KC and Zoe Venditozzi, authors of To Kill a Witch, as they uncover the disturbing reality of Scotland's witch trials. Building on themes of folklore, belief and storytelling touched on throughout The Inverness Castle Experience, this fascinating talk examines the accusations, interrogations, trials and brutal punishments inflicted on almost 4,000 people between 1563 and 1736, many of them women accused of crimes they could never have committed.

Through fascinating research, sharp wit and compelling storytelling, discover how suspicion became accusation, accusation became crime, and crime could lead to the ultimate punishment.

A thought-provoking afternoon of crime, punishment, witchcraft and justice, with a haunting question: could it happen again?

title: Stories from Castle Hill: Tales of the Jacobite Risings
description:
An Infestation of Highlanders

Join Highland Archive Service Community Engagement Officer Lorna Steele-McGinn for an illustrated history talk in the North Tower Bar at The Inverness Castle Experience, as part of Stories from Castle Hill.

This talk explores both the everyday and the seismic events that have shaped the story and image of Inverness and the wider Highlands.

The religious and cultural conflicts of the 17th and 18th centuries transformed Britain and Ireland, culminating in the Battle of Culloden, the last battle fought on British soil. This talk explores the dramatic events of the Jacobite Risings, tracing the story of the Highlands from 1688 to 1746 and examining the people, places and conflicts that left a lasting mark on the region's history.

Relax in the North Tower Bar while enjoying an engaging afternoon of local history and storytelling.

Ticket price includes tea or coffee and a scone.

Please note: This event ticket does not include admission to the main Experience.

title: Spirit Cèilidh
description:
Celebrate the Spirit of St Andrew's Day at the Saltire Bistro with Spirit Cèilidh, an evening of traditional Scottish music, dancing and good company.

Enjoy a hearty serving of stovies before taking to the floor for a lively cèilidh, with experienced callers on hand to guide you through the dances. Whether you're a seasoned dancer or trying it for the first time, gather with friends, meet new people and enjoy a warm Highland welcome as we celebrate Scotland's national day together.

Ticket includes stovies and cèilidh entertainment.

title: A Festive Gathering at the Castle
description:
Join The Inverness Castle Experience for an elegant festive afternoon in the spectacular North Tower Bar.

Guests will gather with a festive cocktail before enjoying a selection of beautifully hand-crafted canapés, accompanied by a seasonal soundtrack of music, festive décor and warm Highland hospitality. A seasonal celebration offering a relaxed and stylish alternative to a traditional Christmas dinner.

The North Tower Bar provides the perfect setting to raise a glass, share stories and celebrate the most wonderful time of the year. Whether you're marking the end of a successful year with colleagues, entertaining valued clients, or simply gathering with friends and loved ones, our Festive Gathering at the Castle is all about celebrating exceptional food and memorable moments.

As the castle sparkles with the Spirit of the season, enjoy an afternoon filled with laughter, conversation and a touch of Christmas magic in one of Inverness' most unique settings.

Festive cocktails. Exceptional canapés. A cosy atmosphere. Christmas, without the formalities.

Inspired by the Spirit of the cèilidh, gathering people together to celebrate and enjoy good company, it's the perfect way to embrace the season. You'll leave with a beautiful handcrafted wreath to display at home and a little extra festive magic to take with you.

title: Stories from Castle Hill: William Fraser Tytler
description:
Join Highland Archive Service Community Engagement Officer Lorna Steele-McGinn for an illustrated history talk exploring the life of William Fraser Tytler and the events, both everyday and extraordinary, that helped shape the story and image of Inverness and the wider Highlands.

Writer, historian, lecturer, lawyer and sheriff, William Fraser Tytler led a remarkable and complex life. His travels took him across the Highlands, where he intervened in famine-stricken communities and played a significant role in the development of the region. He inherited enslaved people on a Jamaican plantation and later instigated the construction of the present-day Inverness Castle in the 1830s and 1840s, helping to create one of the city's most recognisable landmarks and leaving a legacy that continues to shape Inverness today.

Tea, coffee and a scone are included.

description:

Join Highland Archive Service Community Engagement Officer Lorna Steele-McGinn for a series of illustrated history talks focusing on both the everyday and the seismic events which have shaped the story and the image of Inverness and the wider Highlands.

It was the skills and experience of Highland gamekeepers that led to the creation of the Lovat Scouts during the Boer War. It was the specific terrain of Lochaber that made the area perfect for training commandos during WWII. No wonder a large swathe of the Highlands was repeatedly designated a special military area…
